name: CBDT ITR-1 Validation Rules AY 2024-25 (starter)
description: Representative subset of the ITR-1 AY 2024-25 rule set: full Part B/C/D computation chain, Schedule 80D, Schedule 80GGC, taxes paid, identity formats. Severity: Category A scenarios → error.

rules.name: Gross salary (B1(i)) = 17(1) + 17(2) + 17(3) + 89A notified country + 89A other country
rules.group: Part B – Salary and other sources (dropdowns)

rules.name: Allowances exempt u/s 10 (B1ii) = sum of the individual exempt allowances
Net salary (B1iii) = gross salary (B1i) − allowances exempt u/s 10 (B1ii) − relief u/s 89A (B1iia)
rules.notes: Income claimed for relief u/s 89A (B1iia) is also subtracted, as per the form (iii = i − ii − iia).

rules.name: Standard deduction u/s 16(ia) ≤ lower of Rs 50,000 and net salary
rules.notes: "Total salary" read as net salary (B1iii), the amount from which the deduction is made.

rules.name: Deductions u/s 16 (B1 iv) = standard deduction + entertainment allowance + professional tax
Income chargeable under Salaries (B1v) = net salary (B1iii) − deductions u/s 16 (B1iv)
Annual value (B2iii) = gross rent (B2i) − tax paid to local authorities (B2ii)
Standard deduction (B2iv) = 30% of annual value (B2iii)
rules.notes: A negative annual value gives no 30% deduction.

rules.name: Income under House Property (B2vii) = B2iii − B2iv − B2v + B2vi
Income from other sources (B3) = sum of the individual other-source incomes
Deduction u/s 57(iia) only when family pension is offered under other sources
rules.notes: Family pension = other-sources rows with nature FAP.

rules.name: Deduction u/s 57(iia) ≤ lower of 1/3rd of family pension and Rs 15,000
rules.notes: +1 rounding allowance on the one-third.

rules.name: Old regime: gross total income = salary + house property + other sources
rules.notes: Other sources taken net of deduction u/s 57(iia) and relief u/s 89A (the two "Less" lines under B3), because B3 itself is the gross dropdown total (Sl. 40).

rules.name: Default (new) regime with house property loss: gross total income = salary + other sources (loss ignored)
rules.notes: Loss under house property cannot be set off against other heads u/s 115BAC. Other sources net of 57(iia) and 89A relief (see Sl. 7).

rules.name: Default (new) regime with positive house property income: gross total income = salary + house property + other sources
rules.notes: Other sources net of 57(iia) and 89A relief (see Sl. 7).

rules.name: Exempt income total = sum of the individual exempt incomes
80D: preventive health check-up (all four fields together) ≤ Rs 5,000
80D 1a = health insurance premium (i) + preventive check-up (ii), capped at Rs 25,000
rules.notes: The cap is folded into the equality so an above-cap break-up with a capped 1a passes.

rules.name: 80D 1b (self & family, senior citizen) ≤ Rs 50,000
80D 1b = premium (i) + check-up (ii) + medical expenditure (iii), capped at Rs 50,000
80D 2a (parents) ≤ Rs 25,000
80D 2a = premium (i) + preventive check-up (ii), capped at Rs 25,000
80D 2b (parents, senior citizen) ≤ Rs 50,000
80D 2b = premium (i) + check-up (ii) + medical expenditure (iii), capped at Rs 50,000
rules.notes: The document checks the equality only below Rs 50,000; folding the cap into min() is equivalent.

rules.name: 80D 3 eligible amount ≤ Rs 1,00,000
80D 3 eligible amount = 1a + 1b + 2a + 2b, capped at Rs 1,00,000 and at gross total income
Deduction u/s 80GGC in Part C = eligible amount of contribution in Schedule 80GGC
rules.notes: Old regime only (s.115BAC(2)); see rule Aderived80GGC-sch.

rules.name: 80GGC: eligible amount per row = lower of contribution in other mode and gross total income
80GGC: total contribution = contribution in cash + contribution in other mode
80GGC: total eligible amount = sum of the rows’ eligible amounts, restricted to gross total income
Total of deductions claimed (user block) = sum of the individual claimed amounts
rules.notes: UsrDeductUndChapVIA holds the amounts as typed; its total is a plain sum (the GTI restriction applies to DeductUndChapVIA, Sl. 112).

rules.name: Deductions u/s 80C + 80CCC + 80CCD(1) ≤ Rs 1,50,000
Deduction u/s 80TTA ≤ Rs 10,000
Deduction u/s 80TTA ≤ interest from savings account under other sources
rules.notes: Savings interest = other-sources rows with nature SAV.

rules.name: Senior citizen cannot claim deduction u/s 80TTA (80TTB applies instead)
rules.notes: Senior = 60 or more during FY 2023-24, i.e. DOB on or before 1964-04-01 (the document's "on or after 02.04.1964" is the non-senior side).

rules.name: Deduction u/s 80TTB ≤ Rs 50,000
Deduction u/s 80TTB only for senior citizens (DOB on or before 1964-04-01)
Total Chapter VI-A deductions (B5) = sum of the individual deductions, restricted to gross total income
Total income = Gross total income − total Chapter VI-A deductions (not below zero)
rules.notes: Tolerance ±5: total income is rounded to the nearest Rs 10 (s.288A).

rules.name: Total income cannot exceed Rs 50 lakh in ITR-1
Old regime: rebate u/s 87A not available when total income exceeds Rs 5,00,000
Old regime: rebate u/s 87A cannot exceed Rs 12,500 (nor the tax payable)
rules.notes: The rebate is also capped at the tax payable on total income (D1) since it cannot create a negative tax.

rules.name: New regime: rebate u/s 87A above Rs 7,00,000 limited to marginal relief (tax − excess income over 7 lakh)
rules.notes: Marginal rebate (proviso to s.87A): when total income exceeds 7 lakh the rebate cannot exceed tax payable minus the excess of income over 7 lakh; beyond ~7.28 lakh this forces the rebate to zero.

rules.name: New regime: rebate u/s 87A cannot exceed Rs 25,000 (nor the tax payable)
Tax after rebate (D3) = tax payable on total income (D1) − rebate u/s 87A (D2)
Health & education cess (D4) = 4% of tax after rebate (D3)
rules.notes: Derived from the form: ITR-1 has no surcharge, so cess is 4% of D3 (±1 for rounding).

rules.name: Total tax and cess (D5) = tax after rebate (D3) + health & education cess (D4)
Balance tax after relief (D7) = total tax and cess (D5) − relief u/s 89 (D6)
rules.notes: Derived from the form arithmetic; together with Sl. 15 and Sl. 66 this keeps D5–D9 consistent.

rules.name: Total interest and fee payable (D8) = 234A + 234B + 234C + 234F
Total tax, fee and interest (D9) = D5 + 234A + 234B + 234C + 234F − relief u/s 89 (D6)
Total tax, fee and interest (D9) = balance tax after relief (D7) + total interest and fee (D8)
No late filing fee u/s 234F when the return is filed within the due date (139(1))
Late filing fee u/s 234F cannot exceed Rs 5,000 (Rs 1,000 when total income ≤ Rs 5 lakh)
Schedule IT: total tax paid = sum of col 4 of all challans
rules.group: Schedules IT / TDS / TCS – Taxes paid details

rules.name: Schedule TDS1: total tax deducted = sum of the rows
rules.group: Schedules IT / TDS / TCS – Taxes paid details

rules.name: Schedule TDS2: total TDS credit claimed this year (col 6) = sum of the rows
rules.group: Schedules IT / TDS / TCS – Taxes paid details

rules.name: Schedule TDS3: total TDS credit claimed this year (col 6) = sum of the rows
rules.group: Schedules IT / TDS / TCS – Taxes paid details

rules.name: Schedule TCS: total TCS credit claimed this year (col 6) = sum of the rows
rules.group: Schedules IT / TDS / TCS – Taxes paid details

rules.name: Advance tax (D10a) = Schedule IT payments dated 01-04-2023 to 31-03-2024
rules.group: Part D – Taxes paid and refund

rules.name: Self-assessment tax (D10d) = Schedule IT payments dated after 31-03-2024
rules.group: Part D – Taxes paid and refund

rules.name: TDS claimed (D10b) = total TDS claimed in Schedules TDS1 + TDS2 + TDS3
rules.group: Part D – Taxes paid and refund

rules.name: TCS claimed (D10c) = total TCS claimed in Schedule TCS
rules.group: Part D – Taxes paid and refund

rules.name: Total taxes paid (D10) = advance tax + TDS + TCS + self-assessment tax
rules.group: Part D – Taxes paid and refund

rules.name: Total taxes paid (D10) = Schedule IT + TDS1 + TDS2 + TDS3 + TCS totals
rules.notes: The scenario text lists IT, TDS1, TDS2 and TCS; Schedule TDS3 (Form 26QC) is also part of the TDS claimed in ITR-1 and is included so that the totals reconcile.
rules.group: Part D – Taxes paid and refund

rules.name: Refund (D12) = total taxes paid (D10) − total tax, fee and interest (D9), when positive
rules.notes: Refund is 0 (not negative) when taxes paid fall short of the liability. Tolerance ±5: the refund is rounded to the nearest Rs 10 (s.288B).
rules.group: Part D – Taxes paid and refund

rules.name: Amount payable (D11) = total tax, fee and interest (D9) − total taxes paid (D10), when positive
rules.notes: Amount payable is 0 (not negative) when taxes paid exceed the liability. Tolerance ±5: the amount is rounded to the nearest Rs 10 (s.288B).
rules.group: Part D – Taxes paid and refund

rules.name: Schedule IT: a challan for AY 2024-25 cannot be dated before 01-04-2023
rules.notes: Implied by Sl. 205/206: a payment dated before the previous year is neither advance tax nor self-assessment tax, so Sl. 198 (D10 = Schedule IT + TDS + TCS) could not hold.
rules.group: Part D – Taxes paid and refund

rules.name: PAN must be an individual PAN (4th character P) – ITR-1 is for individuals only
rules.notes: The "role CD" of the PAN is its 4th character (P = individual). Full role check against the PAN master is external.

rules.name: IFSC must be in the RBI format (4 letters, 0, 6 alphanumerics)
rules.notes: Partial: matching against the RBI IFSC master needs external data; only the format is checked offline.
rules.group: Part D – Taxes paid and refund

rules.name: Other sources: "Interest from savings bank account" cannot be selected more than once
rules.notes: Dropdown code SAV; the condition restricts the uniqueness check to that code so "OTH" rows may repeat.
rules.group: Part B – Salary and other sources (dropdowns)

rules.name: Other sources: "Interest from deposits (bank / post office / co-operative society)" cannot be selected more than once
rules.notes: Dropdown code IFD; the condition restricts the uniqueness check to that code so "OTH" rows may repeat.
rules.group: Part B – Salary and other sources (dropdowns)

rules.name: Schedule TDS2: TDS claimed this year (col 6) cannot exceed tax deducted (col 5)
rules.group: Schedules IT / TDS / TCS – Taxes paid details

rules.name: PAN in verification must equal the assessee PAN when verifying as Self

computations.name: Gross salary (B1i) = 17(1) + 17(2) + 17(3) + 89A income
Total exempt allowances u/s 10 (B1ii) = sum of the dropdown rows
Net salary (B1iv) = gross salary − exempt allowances − relief 89A
Standard deduction u/s 16(ia) = lower of Rs 50,000 and net salary
computations.notes: Sl. 63 sets the ceiling; the utility always allows the full ceiling, so it is computed.

computations.name: Deductions u/s 16 (B1v) = 16(ia) + 16(ii) + 16(iii)
Income chargeable under Salaries (B1vi) = net salary − deductions u/s 16
Annual value (B2iii) = gross rent − tax paid to local authorities
Standard deduction u/s 24(a) (B2iv) = 30% of annual value
computations.notes: A negative annual value gives no 30% deduction.

computations.name: Income from house property (B2) = annual value − 30% − interest + arrears/unrealised rent
Income from other sources (B3) = sum of the dropdown rows
Deduction u/s 57(iia) = lower of one-third of family pension and Rs 15,000
computations.notes: Sl. 41/42 set the limits (nil without family pension, ≤ 1/3 and ≤ 15,000); the utility allows the full limit.

computations.name: Gross total income (B4) = salary + house property + other sources (a house-property loss is ignored in the new regime)
Total exempt income (agricultural / others) = sum of rows
80D self & family (non-senior) = premium + check-up, max Rs 25,000
80D self & family (senior) = premium + check-up + medical expenditure, max Rs 50,000
80D parents (non-senior) = premium + check-up, max Rs 25,000
80D parents (senior) = premium + check-up + medical expenditure, max Rs 50,000
80D eligible amount = sum of the four limbs, max Rs 1,00,000 and GTI
80GGC row: total contribution = cash + other mode
80GGC row: eligible amount = contribution in other mode (cash not allowed), max GTI
80GGC total in cash = sum of rows
80GGC total in other mode = sum of rows
80GGC total contributions = sum of rows
80GGC total eligible = sum of rows, max GTI
Total deductions claimed (user column) = sum of sections
80C allowed = claim, max Rs 1,50,000 (old regime only)
computations.ref: CBDT ITR-1 AY2024-25 Sl. 91; statutory allocation 80C → 80CCC → 80CCD(1)

computations.name: 80D allowed = claim, max eligible amount in Schedule 80D (old regime only)
80GGC allowed = total eligible in Schedule 80GGC (old regime only)
computations.notes: Old regime only (s.115BAC(2)); in the default regime the schedule must be blank.

computations.name: 80TTA allowed = claim, max Rs 10,000 and savings interest; not for senior citizens (old regime only)
Total deductions allowed (C20) = sum of sections, max GTI
Total income (C21) = gross total income − deductions allowed
Tax payable on total income (D1) at slab rates for the chosen regime
computations.expression: round(if(ITR.ITR1.FilingStatus.OptOutNewTaxRegime == "Y", if(ITR.ITR1.ITR1_IncomeDeductions.TotalIncome <= if(ITR.ITR1.PersonalInfo.DOB <= "1944-04-01", 500000, if(ITR.ITR1.PersonalInfo.DOB <= "1964-04-01", 300000, 250000)), 0, if(ITR.ITR1.ITR1_IncomeDeductions.TotalIncome <= 500000, 0.05 * (ITR.ITR1.ITR1_IncomeDeductions.TotalIncome - if(ITR.ITR1.PersonalInfo.DOB <= "1944-04-01", 500000, if(ITR.ITR1.PersonalInfo.DOB <= "1964-04-01", 300000, 250000))), if(ITR.ITR1.ITR1_IncomeDeductions.TotalIncome <= 1000000, 0.05 * (500000 - if(ITR.ITR1.PersonalInfo.DOB <= "1944-04-01", 500000, if(ITR.ITR1.PersonalInfo.DOB <= "1964-04-01", 300000, 250000))) + 0.2 * (ITR.ITR1.ITR1_IncomeDeductions.TotalIncome - 500000), 0.05 * (500000 - if(ITR.ITR1.PersonalInfo.DOB <= "1944-04-01", 500000, if(ITR.ITR1.PersonalInfo.DOB <= "1964-04-01", 300000, 250000))) + 100000 + 0.3 * (ITR.ITR1.ITR1_IncomeDeductions.TotalIncome - 1000000)))), if(ITR.ITR1.ITR1_IncomeDeductions.TotalIncome <= 300000, 0, if(ITR.ITR1.ITR1_IncomeDeductions.TotalIncome <= 600000, 0.05 * (ITR.ITR1.ITR1_IncomeDeductions.TotalIncome - 300000), if(ITR.ITR1.ITR1_IncomeDeductions.TotalIncome <= 900000, 15000 + 0.1 * (ITR.ITR1.ITR1_IncomeDeductions.TotalIncome - 600000), if(ITR.ITR1.ITR1_IncomeDeductions.TotalIncome <= 1200000, 45000 + 0.15 * (ITR.ITR1.ITR1_IncomeDeductions.TotalIncome - 900000), if(ITR.ITR1.ITR1_IncomeDeductions.TotalIncome <= 1500000, 90000 + 0.2 * (ITR.ITR1.ITR1_IncomeDeductions.TotalIncome - 1200000), 150000 + 0.3 * (ITR.ITR1.ITR1_IncomeDeductions.TotalIncome - 1500000))))))))
computations.ref: Statutory slab rates (Finance Act 2023, s.115BAC); rule Aderivedslab-old / -new
computations.notes: Old regime: basic exemption Rs 2.5 lakh (3 lakh senior, 5 lakh super senior), 5% / 20% / 30%. New regime: 0–3 lakh nil, 5% / 10% / 15% / 20% / 30%. ITR-1 has no special-rate income and no surcharge (total income ≤ 50 lakh).

computations.name: Rebate u/s 87A (D2): old regime up to Rs 12,500 if total income ≤ 5 lakh; new regime up to Rs 25,000 if ≤ 7 lakh, with marginal relief above 7 lakh
